minutes.headline: Commission agreed to draft a private-use plan to save the Brooks House and approved two simple siding/trim applications.
minutes.summary: The Architectural Preservation District Commission took up two determinations of applicability (920 and 61 Main Street), with approval motions made on each. Most of the meeting went to a proposal to preserve the Brooks House through private use, concern over stalled Town Hall and Ritter building repairs and cost estimates, a draft letter and brochure for property owners, and a Historical Commission update.

public_comment.topic: A general contractor described replacing rotted siding at 920 with cedar bevel siding, primed and painted, with no vinyl.
A resident at 912 asked how the commission treats modern materials such as PVC for rotted trim on a historic house.

votes.motion: Approve the determination of applicability for the siding work at 920.
Approve the 61 Main Street determination of applicability (moved and seconded by members).

budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said he would ask the town clerk to refund the application fee the applicant had paid, since a determination of applicability carries no fee.

budget_items.topic: Ritter building and Town Hall repair estimates
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said the original appropriation was roughly a quarter million and the Town Hall bids exceeded the estimate; he asked the town to update the Ritter estimate.
A member said ARPA money must be obligated by the end of 2024 and waiting for a November special town meeting would be too late.
Members discussed paying a designer for a brochure using unspent commission funds, with a minimum print run mentioned.

decisions.decision: Nathan will put together an outline of a plan to preserve the Brooks House through private use for the commission to discuss.
Members agreed to involve the planning board, select board, building reuse committee and historical commission in the Brooks House discussion.
Members supported taking the request for an updated Ritter/Town Hall cost estimate and repair itemized list to the select board.
Members to send comments on the draft property-owner letter within two weeks; final version to be voted on and finalized at the July meeting.
The July meeting date was discussed because of a member's conflict on 11 July; no new date confirmed in captions.

what_happened.line: The commission asked Nathan to draft an outline of a plan to preserve the Brooks House through private use, and agreed to involve four other town bodies.
Members agreed to take a request for an updated Ritter building and Town Hall repair estimate, with an itemized list, to the select board.
A motion to approve the siding determination of applicability at 920 was made; the outcome is not audible in the captions.
The 61 Main Street determination of applicability was moved and seconded, and the chair said it was approved.
Members have two weeks to send comments on a draft property-owner letter; the final version is to be voted on at the July meeting.

why_it_matters: Brooks House is a historic building, and a plan that relies on private use would shift its preservation away from town spending, a choice other town boards would be asked to weigh in on.

Stalled Town Hall and Ritter repairs, and a deadline on federal pandemic-relief (ARPA) money, bear on whether the work can be paid for from that source or would have to wait for a later town meeting vote.
The property-owner letter and brochure are aimed at owners in the historic district, who may be asked to follow its review process for exterior work.
watch_next: The July meeting, where the property-owner letter is to be voted on and finalized; the date was not confirmed because of a member's conflict on 11 July.
Nathan's outline of a Brooks House private-use plan, and the select board's response to the Ritter and Town Hall estimate request.
